reviews.note: `user_history[user_id]` is read to build only that call's context, and the current message plus `final_response` snapshot is appended to that same keyed list.
The ReAct signature has no history field, and the `result.trjectory` typo raises before either the current question or reply is appended to the user's store.
The pinned ReAct constructor has no `adapter` parameter, so `booking_react` is never constructed; the candidate also provides no second specialist.
Both ReAct constructors use unsupported `num_steps` instead of `max_iters`, so the outer module cannot instantiate and no nested specialist reply can be returned.
The router extraction is scripted under `answer` although its signature requires `specialist`, and it returns a reply string that `main` immediately treats as an object with `.specialist`.
One `agent` receives calls for `user_abc123`, then `user_xyz789`, then the first ID again; the final email follow-up explicitly depends on that first user's earlier password turns.
The code constructs one `dspy.ReAct` over ask/move/take; its later loops only inspect the trajectory and never dispatch from a model-produced action.
`TravelSpecialist` and `InvoiceSpecialist` are modules that each own a separate ReAct with a concrete business-tool list, with no Avatar or code-execution agent.
The specialist passes unsupported `adapter` to ReAct, preventing construction, and its forward call uses `query` although the declared input is `booking_query`.

The script supplies `question`, `direction`, and `item` under per-step args, leaves dispatch and observation accumulation to ReAct, and reads observations from `result.trajectory` without a manual history string.
Although the intended call sequence is present, the unterminated f-string in `_get_user_history_context` makes the module unparsable, so the demo cannot run.
A single `dspy.ReAct` owns ask/move/take dispatch; the application loop only reads the resulting trajectory and never routes a predicted action.
The planner call is locally scoped under `dspy.context(adapter=dspy.JSONAdapter())`, with no manual structured-output flags and no ChatAdapter override.
`CarpoolAgent` constructs exactly one ReAct with search, select-best, and confirm tools, and contains no application-side tool-call dispatch loop.

The search-tool definition is syntactically split across `def mock_search_ri` and `des`, and `InputField(type=RiderProfile)` does not provide the class-style typed signature annotation required by the evidence.
`InvoiceSpecialist` gives its inner ReAct an empty tool list, so not every specialist owns concrete business methods as required.
The code references nonexistent `pydantic.RiderProfile`, uses invalid signature annotations, and contains a malformed f-string, so no typed rider input or executable Pydantic tool chain exists.
The final scripted extraction uses `thought` rather than the ChainOfThought `reasoning` field shown by the pinned ReAct test, so the DummyLM list is not in the complete expected shape.

The tool lambdas are syntactically invalid because required parameters follow defaults; their declared argument names also do not match the lambda parameters, and no scripted per-tool steps are supplied.
The history-bearing prompt is passed as undeclared `inputs` while the ChainOfThought signature requires `user_query`, so the call cannot receive the stored turns or reach the reply append.
The ReAct signature declares only a `goal` input and no outcome field, and the tool lambdas are syntactically invalid, so it cannot return the claimed trajectory-plus-extracted-output prediction.
